subject: Model fit eval discovery - next steps (open vs proprietary parity)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>, Angela Cho <angela.cho@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit eval discovery - next steps

Hi Samir / Angela — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Summary of requirements:
- Primary goal: validate open-model parity vs PayGrid proprietary baseline on key downstream tasks (invoice extraction, vendor matching).
- Success metrics: macro-F1 + entity extraction accuracy, and latency p95 SLA for request/response on 8k context.
- Data: PayGrid can provide a sanitized sample (~5k rows) or we can run on a smaller obfuscated subset.

Recommended evaluation plan (initial):
1) Baseline runs: run your proprietary baseline on the sanitized sample to get ground-truth metrics (if you can share).
2) Open-model candidates to evaluate: Redwood-open-13B-v2, Llama2-13B-chat-q4_0, MPT-7B-Instruct-8k.
3) Benchmarks: we’ll run the same prompt set and scoring harness to produce accuracy, macro-F1, hallucination rate, and latency p50/p95.
4) Acceptance threshold suggestion: parity = within 2% absolute of proprietary baseline on macro-F1 and no more than 15% increase in p95 latency. (Open to your input.)

Attachments included: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (prompt templates + evaluation labels) and paygrid-benchmark-20260301.csv (example output format).

Next steps / asks:
- Samir: confirm whether you can share a sanitized sample or prefer we run on an obfuscated subset.
- PayGrid: confirm parity threshold (we suggested <=2% macro-F1 gap).
- Redwood: we’ll run the eval and share a parity report with raw metrics and example failures.

Timeline: initial eval (3–5 business days after we have data/sample).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa and Logan for execution and latency checks.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Angela Cho <angela.cho@paygrid.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 10:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Model fit eval discovery - next steps

Thanks Lauren — really helpful recap. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) Data sharing: we prefer to provide a sanitized sample (PII removed) of ~3k rows to start — team is comfortable with that. We’ll need an NDA addendum that specifically covers the sample for the eval.
2) Parity definition: the 2% macro-F1 window sounds reasonable but we also need qualitative checks on hallucination for entity linking (especially tax IDs). Can you include a small manual review step in the report?
3) Latency: our current production p95 for the proprietary baseline is ~260ms. We can tolerate up to 330ms for the open models, but anything above that will require us to consider a hybrid approach.

One ask: can Redwood run the proprietary baseline for comparison if we provide a Docker image or do you need the metrics from our side? Running it on your infra would speed things up but we’re concerned about IP — we can sign a temporary run agreement.

Also, what does the evaluation output look like? Can you share an example report?

If these items look fine I’ll schedule a quick alignment call with engineering next week.

—Samir
Head of AI, PayGrid
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Model fit eval discovery - request: run baseline eval

Folks — forwarding PayGrid’s notes. Key asks:
- They will provide a sanitized sample (~3k rows) and want a parity report (metrics + small manual review).
- They asked whether we can run their proprietary baseline from a Docker image under a run agreement.

Marissa: can you kick off the benchmark runs for the candidate models listed (Redwood-open-13B-v2, Llama2-13B-chat-q4_0, MPT-7B-Instruct-8k) using the attached prompt_set_v1.jsonl and the paygrid-benchmark-20260301.csv schema? Please include hallucination checks and per-entity precision/recall.

Logan: please validate estimated p95 latency for each model on our Dedicated 1 GPU profile and confirm whether we can meet PayGrid’s 330ms tolerance at 8k context. If we need quantized variants, note the quality/latency trade-offs.

Attach: prompt_set_v1.jsonl, paygrid-benchmark-20260301.csv

I’ll coordinate the NDA/run agreement with legal if PayGrid confirms. Marking this as high priority — Samir is aiming to decide by the end of next week.

Thanks,
Lauren
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Model fit eval discovery - request: run baseline eval

Lauren / Logan — plan and timing from the bench team: 

Execution plan:
- Step 1 (Day 0): ingest PayGrid sanitized sample once shared, validate schema, and run quick sanity checks.
- Step 2 (Days 1–3): run candidate models through the evaluation harness (prompt_set_v1.jsonl) to produce metrics: macro-F1, per-entity precision/recall, hallucination flags, and p50/p95 latency under the Dedicated 1 profile.
- Step 3 (Day 3–5): produce parity report with example failure cases and a short manual review (10–15 examples) for hallucination-sensitive entities (tax IDs, vendor names).

Notes on proprietary baseline run:
- We can execute the customer-provided Docker image in an isolated sandbox if PayGrid signs a temporary run agreement and grants the image. If they prefer, they can run the baseline and share metrics; either option is fine but running it here speeds up the cadence.

Acceptance thresholds (proposal):
- Parity = within 2% absolute macro-F1 of proprietary baseline.
- Hallucination: no more than 1.5x the hallucination rate of baseline on manually reviewed samples.
- Latency: p95 <= 330ms (PayGrid tolerance). If open model p95 > 330ms but quality is otherwise within parity, recommend hybrid routing or quantized variants—call out expected cost impact.

Deliverables:
- Raw metric CSV (see paygrid-benchmark-20260301.csv format).
- Parity report PDF with top failure examples and manual-review notes (will post to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-paygrid-evals).
- Short runbook with recommended model variant and deployment plan for production trials.

Timeline estimate: 3–5 business days after we receive sanitized sample and signed run agreement (if PayGrid wants us to run their image).

I’ll start the candidate runs once we get the sample — cc’ing PayGrid contact in the next outbound.

—Marissa
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
